the fate and effects of Ni in salt marsh sediment and the role of AMF in the response of salt marsh plants to heavy metal pollution.

the salt marsh Spartina patens can tolerate moderate levels of Ni, however, at higher levels, the plant is affected by reduced growth, decreased photosynthesis, and reduced transfer efficiency of photosystem II reaction centres, but not by the AMF.

The main takeaway from our work is that
salt marsh plants are able to take up heavy metals from contaminated sediment but that metal translocation to aboveground plant tissue is low and that metal toxicity to plants and AMF is limited.
the fate of metals in restored salt marsh sediments is not significantly influenced by the presence of vegetation and AMF, and that Ni amendment had no long-term effects on the salt marsh ecosystem.
salt marsh plants and AMF are not particularly sensitive to heavy metals, even when exposed to high concentrations of metals.
